p.src: Overview: Scattering reduces a collision to invariant data that can be compared with experiment. For four identical particles those data may be organized into the Mandelstam variables $s,t,u$, only two of which are independent. Ordinary particle exchange then suggests separate direct and crossed channels. The Veneziano amplitude overturned that expectation: one function contains both channel descriptions. The second half of the lecture builds that function from two open strings that join, evolve as one oscillating chain, and split again.

p.src: Fermionic strings solve two defects of the purely bosonic model: they admit fermionic states and, after the appropriate projection, remove the tachyon. p.src: Scattering is not necessarily the most interesting thing particles do. It is simply the operation that an experiment can repeat cleanly. Send specified particles toward one another, record the particles emerging from the collision, and infer the dynamics hidden inside the interaction region. A theory becomes quantitative when it supplies a complex amplitude $\mathcal A(\hbox{incoming data}\to\hbox{outgoing data}),$ whose squared magnitude, together with the usual phase-space factors, gives the probability for that outcome.

Consider two particles entering with momenta $k_1,k_2$ and two leaving with physical momenta $q_3,q_4$. Conservation of energy and momentum is one four-vector equation, $k_1+k_2=q_3+q_4.$ It is convenient to assign an incoming momentum to every external line: $k_3\equiv-q_3,
  \qquad
  k_4\equiv-q_4.$ Then $k_1+k_2+k_3+k_4=0,$ and every leg obeys $k_i^2=-m_i^2$. The outgoing particles have negative energy only in this bookkeeping convention; their physical energies remain positive.

p.src:
At first the amplitude appears to be a function of sixteen components, $\mathcal A(k_1,k_2,k_3,k_4)$. Most of them are redundant. Go to the center-of-mass frame, rotate the incoming momenta onto a chosen axis, and assume for simplicity that all four particles have the same mass. Only their deflection angle $\theta$ remains. The process therefore has two independent kinematic variables: $E_{\mathrm{cm}},
  \qquad
  \theta.$

p.src:
A single pole is a poor model of meson scattering. Two mesons can form many resonances, with a tower of masses and angular momenta. The first response in the 1960s was to add more $s$-channel poles, more $t$-channel poles, and the allowed $u$-channel poles. Then a much more economical function was found. In the lecture’s units, where the linear Regge trajectory and its intercept have been absorbed into $s$ and $t$, it is $\mathcal A_{\mathrm V}(s,t)
  \propto
  \frac{\Gamma(-s)\Gamma(-t)}{\Gamma(-s-t)}.$ The gamma function continues the factorial: $\Gamma(n)=(n-1)!$ at positive integers.

p.src:
Let the first chain have coordinates $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, and the second $x_{n+1},\ldots,x_{2n}$. Their center-of-mass coordinates are $X_{\mathrm{cm}}^{(1)}
  =\frac1n\sum_{a=1}^{n}x_a,
  \qquad
  X_{\mathrm{cm}}^{(2)}
  =\frac1n\sum_{a=n+1}^{2n}x_a.$ A chain with definite momentum $k_1$ has a center-of-mass plane wave multiplied by an internal oscillator ground state: $\begin{aligned}\Psi_1
  &=
  e^{ik_1\cdot X_{\mathrm{cm}}^{(1)}}
  \psi_0(x_1,\ldots,x_n),
  \\
  \Psi_2
  &=
  e^{ik_2\cdot X_{\mathrm{cm}}^{(2)}}
  \psi_0(x_{n+1},\ldots,x_{2n}).
  \end{aligned}$ The factors $\psi_0$ depend on relative coordinates, not on the common translation of an entire chain. Because the incoming strings are initially separate quantum systems, $\Psi_{\mathrm{in}}=\Psi_1\Psi_2.$

p.src: Finding a spin-one or spin-two state in the oscillator spectrum was suggestive, but not decisive. Their scattering amplitudes supplied the stronger test. Photon amplitudes obey the identities associated with charge conservation and gauge invariance; graviton amplitudes obey the corresponding constraints of a massless spin-two field. The string states passed these tests in interactions with massive and massless states and with one another. That is why the photon and graviton labels became physical identifications rather than guesses based only on polarization counting.  (Editorial clarification: In modern language these tests are encoded in decoupling of unphysical polarizations, gauge Ward identities, and the universal low-energy coupling of the massless spin-two state.)

ja: 振動子スペクトルにスピン1またはスピン2の状態を見出すことは示唆的であったが、決定的ではなかった。それらの散乱振幅がより強いテストを与えた。光子振幅は電荷保存とゲージ不変性に関連する恒等式を満たし、重力子振幅は質量ゼロのスピン2場に対応する制約を満たす。弦の状態は、質量のある状態および質量のない状態との相互作用、および互いの相互作用においてこれらのテストに合格した。だからこそ光子と重力子というラベルは、偏極の計数のみに基づく推測ではなく、物理的同定となったのである。  (編集上の補足: 現代的な言葉では、これらのテストは非物理的偏極の脱結合、ゲージ・ウォード恒等式、および質量ゼロのスピン2状態の普遍的低エネルギー結合に符号化されている。)
zh: 在振子谱中发现自旋为一或自旋为二的态是有启发性的，但并非决定性的。它们的散射振幅提供了更强的检验。光子振幅服从与电荷守恒和规范不变性相关的恒等式；引力子振幅服从无质量自旋二场的相应约束。弦态在与有质量和无质量态的相互作用中以及彼此之间的相互作用中通过了这些检验。这就是为什么光子和引力子标签成为物理上的认定，而不是仅基于极化计数的猜测。  (编者说明: 用现代语言来说，这些检验被编码在非物理极化的解耦、规范Ward恒等式以及无质量自旋二态的普适低能耦合中。)
